passes strict admission. Without that artifact, all32 cells remain unsubmitted.

![Historical throughput: eight bars compare Tesseract and Python Indra under shared and partitioned application quotas; no native Rust measurement](../figures/signed-baseline-throughput.png)

![Historical successful-response p95: eight bars, with larger values indicating slower tail latency and no confidence intervals](../figures/signed-baseline-p95.png)

The historical study has 15 mostly English synthetic fixtures, each executed
three times. All eight cells have 45 successful responses. It cannot meet the
new multilingual quality requirement. At one CPU, concurrency was one; at two
CPUs, it was two. That changes both available CPU and offered load. The old load
generator was outside the application cgroup. These results must not be pooled
with the new experiment, which includes its load generator inside the common
CPU and memory limits.

Python Indra's historical shared-quota throughput exceeds its partitioned-quota
throughput. The partitions constrain Tika independently even while OCR quota is
idle; the measurements support investigating that deployment tradeoff. They do
not identify the cause independently of the complete stack. Tail latency worsens
under the partitioned configuration despite a better median. Therefore a single
throughput ratio is insufficient to select a production configuration.

Strict CER was 409/9029 for Tesseract and 131/9029 for Python Indra. The
whitespace-collapsed secondary view was 195/8924 versus 11/8924. These are repeated
measurements of the same 15 references, not 120 independent accuracy samples.
Whitespace materially changes the apparent advantage; strict and collapsed
metrics should remain adjacent in the new analysis.

## Frozen multilingual study

The [main manifest](../corpus-frozen.json) contains 33 primary pages in 19 document
clusters and eight separately reported challenges. The primary appearance mix is
19 printed, 11 handwritten and three mixed pages. English occurs on two primary
pages in one cluster; 51 of 87,515 NFC reference letters are English. All three
proportions are below 10%. This is a small, heterogeneous engineering corpus, not
a representative sample of every language, profession or production deployment.

The [protocol](../protocol.json) fixes Tika rendering, source/model hashes,
configuration identities, warmup, repetition order, CPU/memory policy and metrics
before OCR execution. The Rust evaluator records immutable input/reference and
output identities, HTTP failures and complete-body timing. Execution repetitions
are technical repeats; quality uses the declared first repetition. Paired
resampling draws complete document clusters, preserving within-document
dependence. Language, script, domain, appearance, reference quality and task type
are descriptive strata; small strata do not justify broad inferential claims.

Strict NFC code-point CER retains whitespace and punctuation. A separate
whitespace-collapsed CER qualifies transcription/layout effects. WER uses the
declared whitespace tokenizer and is omitted where that tokenization is
inappropriate. Public training overlap is unknown. Historical editorial
transcriptions and extracted PDF text have explicit reference qualifications.
Oracle crops are challenge inputs, never relabeled as full-page end-to-end OCR.

## Execution admission and all planned statuses

With no artifact supplied, every cell below is explicitly **unsubmitted**. Missing
measurements have no numeric value. To admit downloaded combined evidence, set
`OCR_EVALUATION_ROOT` and the independently selected full commit
`OCR_EVALUATION_SOURCE_SHA` together before rendering. An invalid artifact aborts
this notebook; it never falls back to the historical data or an empty study.

```{python}
import os
import pandas as pd
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", None)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", None)

expected_source = os.environ.get("OCR_EVALUATION_SOURCE_SHA")
study.require(bool(artifact_root) == bool(expected_source), "set both artifact root and source SHA")
new_study = study.load(Path(artifact_root), expected_source) if artifact_root else {
    "statuses": study.missing_cells(), "measurements": [], "comparisons": []
}
pd.DataFrame(new_study["statuses"])
```

The loader verifies the complete SHA inventory, exact frozen studies and seeds,
32 unique cells and 112 comparison identities, reviewer-selected source,
shard/candidate/evaluator bindings, raw journals and outputs, first-attempt
metadata, derived quality summaries, attempt CSVs, complete workload throughput
and unchanged parent CPU/memory quotas. Failed/incomplete cells remain visible
but cannot supply measurements. The artifact inventory checks integrity; release
Cosign verification and the retained live OCI/cgroup acceptance receipts are
separate evidence, not signatures independently checked by this Python loader.

```{python}
coverage = []
for cohort, frozen in study.frozen_studies().items():
    for case in frozen["manifest"]["cases"]:
        coverage.append({"study": cohort, **{k: case[k] for k in
            ("cohort", "language", "script", "domain", "appearance", "reference_quality", "task")},
            "document_cluster": case["document_cluster"]})
coverage_frame = pd.DataFrame(coverage)
coverage_frame.groupby(["study", "cohort", "language", "appearance", "task"], dropna=False).agg(
    cases=("document_cluster", "size"), document_clusters=("document_cluster", "nunique")
).reset_index()
```

Counts describe selection coverage; they are not independent accuracy samples.
Reference-letter denominators require the hash-verified acquired references;
manifest classifications alone cannot independently reproduce their contents.
Unknown model-training overlap, exposed implementation examples and editorial
reference qualifications remain limitations even when every file hash matches.

[all six stratum axes with CER/collapsed CER/eligible WER](study-data/summaries.csv). The
[artist receipt](study-data/plot-validation.json) binds their hashes and verifies
actual Seaborn point positions, values, colors, count labels and frozen interval
endpoints. Missing marks say **no numeric value**; the fast PSM3 comparison row is
a zero identity anchor, with no estimated self-comparison interval.

The compact table below uses the predeclared fast PSM3, Python text and Rust text
arms for readability. The exports retain all eight arms, all six stratum axes and
all three metrics, including tokenizer eligibility and unavailable WER. Values
remain conditional on scoreable first attempts; coverage and failures travel with
each cell. Appearance/language strata describe this finite selection.

```{python}
if new_study["measurements"]:
    strata = pd.read_csv(report_directory / "study-data/summaries.csv")
    focus = ("tesseract-fast-psm3", "python-text-b64", "rust-text-b64")
    selected = strata[(strata.study == "main") & (strata.cohort == "primary") &
                      strata.axis.isin(("appearance", "language")) & (strata.metric == "cer") & strata.variant.isin(focus)].copy()
    def compact(row):
        value = "no numeric" if pd.isna(row.micro_rate) else f"{100 * row.micro_rate:.1f}%"
        return f"{value} · {int(row.scored_cases)}/{int(row.selected_cases)}; F{int(row.service_failures)}; M{int(row.metric_limits)}"
    if not selected.empty:
        selected["strict CER · scored/selected; failures; metric limits"] = selected.apply(compact, axis=1)
        display(selected.pivot(index=["axis", "level", "cpus"], columns="variant", values="strict CER · scored/selected; failures; metric limits").reindex(columns=focus))
```

Strict and collapsed CER remain adjacent. Both condition on scoreable first
attempts; the row labels retain service failures and metric limits. Paired
intervals come unchanged from the Rust scorer's frozen document-cluster draws.
Each pair can use a different joint-success subset; its eligible case/cluster and
reference-unit counts and both arms' exclusions remain visible. A conditional
paired difference is not a whole-arm benefit or a population superiority claim.
The laboratory supplement has no intervals; challenge summaries remain separate
and descriptive. CER may exceed 100%; plots neither cap it nor use logarithmic
axes that would hide zero.

Whole-main throughput covers all 41 primary-plus-challenge cases across all three
technical repetitions; it is not repeated as a primary/language throughput.
Higher throughput and lower latency are favorable. Successful complete-body
latencies use linear type7 empirical quantiles of all admitted successful
non-warmup attempts; they are finite observations, with failed-attempt counts
alongside them. Failed termination times
remain in the raw export. A missing successful sample yields no latency mark.
Neither repetitions nor high quantiles create independent documents or a
production tail guarantee. CPU budgets remain separate; a budget difference is
not by itself isolated CPU scaling.

Tesseract receives the prespecified per-case language hint and PSM; Indra uses its
native script handling without those request headers. Cases include qualified
editorial references and oracle crops; no single quality ranking applies to all
production domains. All arms are serial at concurrency 1; this does not test
cross-request continuous batching. Startup includes Docker create/start and
readiness polling after model-inventory hashing has warmed the file cache; it is
not storage-cold startup or request latency. Parent charged-memory lifetime peaks
include setup/sentinel/startup, while request CPU deltas include warmup. Model
cache pages populated outside the parent can remain charged elsewhere. Shared
3GiB/zero-swap accounting includes Tika, optional OCR and the load generator.
Actual result interpretation and exact-hash full visual review remain pending.

## Laboratory supplement

The [separate Portuguese supplement](../laboratory-supplement/README.md) contains
two chemistry methods crops from distinct public papers. The evaluated crops
contain no English reference letters; their surrounding source pages may contain
English. It is not a collection of complete laboratory reports or clinical
documents. With only two document clusters, the supplement reports descriptive
point estimates and failures, with **zero bootstrap resamples and no confidence
intervals**. The published acquisition amendment preserves original hashes, recovers two
exact HTML originals and retains two changed live responses as audit evidence.
The separately hashed operational acquisition index omits the two unavailable
metadata originals without replacing frozen inputs, references or protocols.

## Remaining report acceptance

The finished notebook must admit only artifact-bound score/performance records,
show every planned/failed/missing cell, preserve failure denominators, display
paired cluster intervals only where the protocol permits them, and distinguish
main primary pages, challenges and laboratory crops. Performance units must match
the measured workload: successful case responses per complete workload second,
with latency conditioned on success and failed-attempt termination reported
separately. No successful-only plot may conceal an arm's failure rate.

Render with a locked reporting environment and a pinned Quarto release. Save the
HTML, figure source data, PNG/SVG exports, source hashes and plot-validation
receipts. Inspect every rendered chart and the complete HTML layout visually.
Rendering a source notebook or checking numeric bar heights alone does not prove
that the final visualization is legible or correctly annotated.
